100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 7, 1926, the world was abuzz with the news of the ongoing political turmoil in Germany, where a new coalition government struggled to maintain stability in the wake of post-war economic challenges. In the United States, the Senate continued debates over the pending tariff bill, which aimed to protect domestic industries amidst growing international competition. Meanwhile, British Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin faced criticism over his handling of the coal miners' strike, as tensions escalated in the mining communities.
